title: Cross-surface launch: traffic shadowing & staged cutover slate
creator: Maya Chen
description: Coordinate a cross-surface launch plan that uses traffic shadowing (mirror traffic), staged cutover windows, and SLO-gated canaries across runtime, console, and API surfaces so we can validate behavior at scale without user-visible regressions.
background: Recent model upgrade and kernel selection changes require validation across multiple front-line surfaces (hosted API, dedicated routing, and console user flows). Prior launches leaned heavily on feature flags and regional rollouts; several teams requested a more repeatable traffic shadowing pattern plus explicit cutover automation to reduce manual ops during launches.
goals: Provide a documented, repeatable pattern for mirrored traffic validation (traffic shadowing) that produces actionable telemetry without impacting end users
Define SLO-based gating (latency, error-rate, cost per token) to automatically advance or rollback canaries
Coordinate windows across runtime, console, and API teams and publish a single-cutover slate with fallbacks
Ship automation artifacts (runbooks, gateway configs, dashboards) so engineering can run launches with minimal bespoke coordination
scope: Design and validate traffic shadowing configuration for API Gateway and runtime router
Create canary gating rules based on latency p99, tail error-rate, and cost delta
Publish a per-region launch calendar and cutover playbook
Instrument dashboards and alerting for shadowed traffic metrics and divergence detection
out_of_scope: Major model architecture changes (these are handled by Model Onboarding team)
Billing system changes for token accounting (billing remains on existing pipeline)
Re-architecting KV cache behavior — we will test as-is and capture regressions
deliverables: Traffic Shadowing runbook (Confluence) with step-by-step gateway commands
SLO gating matrix and automated deploy jobs in CI
Grafana dashboards and alert rules for shadow divergence and cost delta
Cross-team cutover calendar and communications templates

tasks: PM: Draft cross-surface schedule and communications (Maya)
ENG: Implement mirror routing in API Gateway and runtime router (ENG-22841)
ENG: Add tagging to shadowed requests to avoid billing side-effects
Console: Add shadow telemetry hooks for UI flows and enable feature flag for mirrored reads
Infra: Create canary gating job and link to CI/CD (ENG-23199)
DevOps: Prepare fallback routes and capacity reservations for Dedicated pools
SRE: Add alerts and escalations for divergence >5% between shadow and prod responses
PM: Coordinate stakeholder dry-run and tabletop exercises
notes: Stakeholder syncs scheduled Tue/Thu 9am PT for the next 3 weeks
We will avoid mirroring writes to downstream billing and analytics by stripping write headers
Design and legal have reviewed data retention for shadow logs — scope limited to 48h and sampled
Cost estimate: expected 8-12% additional token volume during 24h pilot; finance notified
decisions: Start shadowing at 10% mirrored traffic for pilot — not to exceed 100 RPS per region
SLO gating thresholds: latency p99 <1.5x baseline, tail error-rate delta <0.5%, cost delta <15%
If any gating metric breaches for >15 minutes, automatic rollback and page SRE
Mirror traffic will be instrumented but excluded from customer-facing logs and billing
risks: Telemetry volume from mirrored traffic could overwhelm existing dashboards
Hidden side-effects in downstream systems (analytics, billing) if headers not stripped
Cross-region capacity contention during simultaneous canaries
False positives in divergence detection due to nondeterministic model outputs
mitigations: Add rate-limits and sampling for shadowed traffic; cap to 10% for pilot
Explicit header strip and write-mask in gateway to protect billing/analytics
Stagger regional canary windows and reserve dedicated capacity for canaries
Capture deterministic prompt set for approximate-output comparison and human review workflow

acceptance_criteria: Pilot shadowing runs for 24h in eu-west-1 with no customer-visible regressions
SLO gating job correctly advances/rolls back based on defined thresholds during canary
Dashboards show mirror divergence metrics and alerts fire at configured thresholds
Cutover runbook validated in a tabletop drill and signed off by SRE and Legal
